faq.question: What affects livestock prices in Kenya?
faq.answer: Prices vary by animal condition/weight, breed, season (prices spike before Eid, Christmas, Easter), drought conditions (supply increase = lower prices), and market location.

faq.question: Where is the biggest livestock market in Kenya?
faq.answer: Dagoretti Market in Nairobi is the largest urban livestock market. For pastoral areas, Garissa and Isiolo are major trading hubs.

faq.question: How do I sell livestock at a market?
faq.answer: Bring your animals to the market on designated market days. You'll need a livestock movement permit from your local veterinary officer. Buyers negotiate directly with sellers.

faq.question: How can I identify which network a Kenyan phone number belongs to?
faq.answer: Look at the first 4 digits of the number (e.g. 0722). Safaricom uses 0700–0729, 0740–0743, 0790–0799, 0110–0119 among others. Airtel uses 0730–0739, 0750–0756, 0780–0789, 0100–0109. Telkom uses 0770–0779, 0120–0129.

faq.question: What is Kenya's country code?
faq.answer: Kenya's country code is +254. When dialing a Kenyan number internationally, drop the leading 0 and add +254. Example: 0722 123 456 becomes +254 722 123 456.

faq.question: What prefixes does Faiba use?
faq.answer: Faiba (Jamii Telecoms) uses the prefix 0747. They primarily focus on data services and mobile broadband.

faq.question: Can a number switch between networks?
faq.answer: Yes, Kenya supports Mobile Number Portability (MNP), meaning users can switch networks while keeping their number. However, the prefix will still show the original network allocation.

faq.answer: M-Pesa charges vary by amount and whether the recipient is registered. Sending to a registered user ranges from KES 0 (for amounts under KES 100) to KES 108 (for amounts over KES 25,000). Sending to unregistered users costs more.

faq.question: What is the M-Pesa maximum transaction limit?
faq.answer: The maximum single M-Pesa transaction is KES 250,000. The maximum daily transaction total is KES 500,000, and the maximum M-Pesa account balance is KES 500,000.

faq.answer: Use Buy Goods (Lipa Na M-Pesa) whenever possible as it's free. When sending money, check the fee boundaries — sometimes sending KES 500 instead of KES 501 can save you fees because of tariff band transitions.

faq.question: How much does it cost to enter a national park in Kenya?
faq.answer: Entry fees vary by park and visitor category. Kenyan citizens pay KES 200–500/day, residents KES 400–2,500/day, and non-residents USD 15–90/day. Children pay approximately half. Premium parks like Maasai Mara and Amboseli charge more.

faq.question: What is the difference between a national park and a national reserve?
faq.answer: National parks are managed by Kenya Wildlife Service (KWS) with no human settlement or grazing allowed. National reserves are managed by county governments and may allow some pastoral activities.

faq.question: What is the Big Five?
faq.answer: The Big Five are: Lion, Leopard, Elephant, Rhinoceros, and Cape Buffalo. The best parks to see all five include Maasai Mara, Lake Nakuru, and Ol Pejeta Conservancy.

faq.question: When is the best time for safari in Kenya?
faq.answer: The dry season (June–October) is best for wildlife viewing as animals gather around water sources. The Great Wildebeest Migration crosses into Maasai Mara from July–October. However, the green season (November–May) offers lower rates and fewer crowds.

faq.question: How do I book a KWS park visit?
faq.answer: You can book through the eCitizen portal (ecitizen.go.ke) or pay at the gate. For popular parks, advance booking is recommended, especially during peak season (July–October and December–January).

faq.question: What is NHIF accreditation?
faq.answer: NHIF accreditation means a hospital or clinic has been approved by the National Hospital Insurance Fund to provide healthcare services to NHIF members. Only accredited facilities can accept NHIF cover directly.

faq.question: What does hospital level mean in Kenya?
faq.answer: Kenya's health system has 6 levels: Level 1 (community), Level 2 (dispensary), Level 3 (health centre), Level 4 (sub-county hospital with surgery), Level 5 (county referral with specialists), Level 6 (national referral — KNH, MTRH).

faq.question: Can I use NHIF at a private hospital?
faq.answer: Yes, many private hospitals are NHIF-accredited. However, NHIF cover at private facilities may require a co-payment for services that exceed NHIF rebate limits.

faq.question: Has NHIF transitioned to SHA / SHIF?
faq.answer: Yes, the Social Health Authority (SHA) and Social Health Insurance Fund (SHIF) officially replaced NHIF on October 1, 2024 under the Social Health Insurance Act 2023. faq.question: How do I check if my hospital is NHIF-accredited?
faq.answer: You can check at nhif.or.ke or call the NHIF toll-free line 0800 720 601. This tool also lists major accredited facilities across Kenya.

faq.question: What do Kenya number plate prefixes mean?
faq.answer: Kenya plates follow the format KXX 000X (3-letter prefix, 3 digits, 1 letter). The prefix historically indicated the county of registration and approximate year. Since most registrations now happen centrally in Nairobi, newer prefixes mainly indicate the year of registration.

faq.question: What does GK mean on a Kenya plate?
faq.answer: GK stands for 'Government of Kenya' and is used on all central government vehicles. These plates are white with blue text.

faq.question: What is a CD number plate in Kenya?
faq.answer: CD plates belong to diplomatic corps (foreign embassies and consulates). The number after CD indicates the country. CC plates are for consular corps.

faq.question: Why are letters I and O missing from Kenya plates?
faq.answer: The letters I and O are omitted from Kenya registration plate prefixes to avoid confusion with the numbers 1 and 0.

faq.question: Can I get a personalized number plate in Kenya?
faq.answer: Yes, NTSA offers personalized/vanity plates for an additional fee. However, these plates cannot be decoded to determine registration county or year.

faq.question: How long does it take to get a Kenyan passport?
faq.answer: The official processing time is 10–15 working days after biometric capture. However, wait times can sometimes be longer depending on backlog. An expedited/emergency passport takes 1–3 days.

faq.question: How much does it cost to replace a lost National ID?
faq.answer: Replacement of a lost or damaged National ID is currently free under the government fee waiver. A lost ID still requires a police abstract, while a damaged ID should be surrendered. Confirm the waiver is still active before applying.

faq.question: How do I apply for a passport in Kenya?
faq.answer: The entire process starts online via the eCitizen portal. You fill out the application, pay the fees, and book an appointment. Then you visit the Immigration office or Huduma Centre on your appointment date with original documents for biometrics.

faq.question: Can I get a passport for my child?
faq.answer: Yes, Kenyan citizens under 18 can apply for a passport through eCitizen. The application must be made with a parent or legal guardian and the current fee should be confirmed in eCitizen before payment.

faq.question: What PAYE tax bands apply in Kenya?
faq.answer: Kenya uses progressive tax bands: 10% for the first KES 24,000, 25% for KES 24,001–32,333, 30% for KES 32,334–500,000, 32.5% for KES 500,001–800,000, and 35% above KES 800,000. A personal relief of KES 2,400 per month is applied.

faq.question: Is the Affordable Housing Levy mandatory?
faq.answer: Yes, since the Finance Act 2023 and the Supreme Court ruling upholding it, all employed persons pay 1.5% of gross salary as the Affordable Housing Levy. The employer also contributes 1.5%. Under the Tax Laws (Amendment) Act, 2024, the employee's Housing Levy and SHIF contributions are full pre-tax allowable deductions.

faq.question: What are the new NSSF rates in Kenya?
faq.answer: Under the NSSF Act 2013 (now in effect), employees contribute 6% of pensionable pay. Under the Year 4 schedule (effective February 2026), Tier I covers up to KES 9,000 (max KES 540) and Tier II covers KES 9,001–108,000 (max KES 5,940; total max KES 6,480/month). The employer matches these contributions.

faq.question: How is SHA calculated in Kenya?
faq.answer: The Social Health Insurance Fund contribution is calculated at 2.75% of gross salary and is remitted through the Social Health Authority. It replaced the former NHIF income bands.

faq.question: How do I verify if a professional is registered in Kenya?
faq.answer: Each regulatory body has a public register or verification portal. Use the verification URL provided for each body in our directory. For doctors, check kmpdc.go.ke; for lawyers, check lsk.or.ke/find-a-lawyer.

faq.question: Is professional registration mandatory in Kenya?
faq.answer: Yes, practising a regulated profession without valid registration is a criminal offence under the respective Acts. This applies to doctors, lawyers, engineers, accountants, nurses, and many other professions.

faq.question: How much does professional registration cost?
faq.answer: Costs vary widely — from KES 1,000 (TSC for teachers) to KES 20,000+ (CMA for investment advisors). Most bodies charge KES 3,000–10,000 for initial registration plus annual renewal fees.

notes: Under Section 4 of the Public Holidays Act (Cap 110), when a public holiday falls on a Sunday, the following Monday is observed as a public holiday.
Islamic holidays (Eid ul-Fitr and Eid ul-Adha) depend on the sighting of the moon and are formally gazetted by the Cabinet Secretary for Interior.
Mazingira Day (10 October) was amended from Utamaduni/Huduma Day in 2024 to dedicate the holiday to national tree planting and environmental conservation.

faq.question: How many public holidays does Kenya have?
faq.answer: Kenya has approximately 11–13 gazetted public holidays per year. The exact number varies because Islamic holidays (Eid ul-Fitr, Eid ul-Adha) are determined by moon sighting. Additionally, if a holiday falls on a Sunday, Monday is observed.

faq.question: What happens when a public holiday falls on a Sunday?
faq.answer: When a gazetted public holiday falls on a Sunday, the following Monday is automatically observed as a public holiday. This is specified in the Public Holidays Act (Cap 110).

faq.question: Are Islamic holidays public holidays in Kenya?
faq.answer: Yes, Eid ul-Fitr (end of Ramadan) and Eid ul-Adha (Festival of Sacrifice) are gazetted public holidays in Kenya. Their exact dates depend on the Islamic lunar calendar and moon sighting.

faq.question: What is Mashujaa Day?
faq.answer: Mashujaa Day (Heroes' Day) is celebrated on October 20th. It honors all Kenyans who contributed to the struggle for independence and the development of the nation. It replaced Kenyatta Day in 2010.

faq.question: Can the President declare additional public holidays?
faq.answer: Yes, the President of Kenya can declare additional public holidays through a gazette notice. This has been done for events like elections, national mourning, and special national occasions.

It is illegal to act as an estate agent without EARB registration — Section 4 of the Act
Registered agents must renew their license annually by March 31
Always insist on seeing an agent's EARB registration certificate before engaging their services

faq.question: Why must a real estate agent be registered?
faq.answer: Under the Estate Agents Act (Cap 533), it is illegal to practice as an estate agent in Kenya without being registered with the Estate Agents Registration Board (EARB). Registration ensures the agent is qualified and holds a fidelity guarantee bond to protect clients from fraud.

faq.question: What is the Estate Agents Registration Board (EARB)?
faq.answer: EARB is the regulatory body established by law to register estate agents, regulate their practice, and protect the public from unscrupulous agents in Kenya.

faq.question: How do I check if an agent is registered?
faq.answer: Ask for their EARB registration certificate and verify their name or registration number on the official EARB website register (earb.go.ke). The certificate must be valid for the current year.

faq.question: What happens if I use an unregistered agent?
faq.answer: If you use an unregistered agent, you have no legal recourse through EARB if you are defrauded. Unregistered agents are also not bound by professional ethics or required to hold insurance bonds to protect client money.

notes: All public primary, junior secondary, and senior secondary schools follow the Ministry of Education gazetted calendar.
Term 3 has no mid-term break in order to accommodate national examinations (KPSEA, KJSEA, and KCSE) in late October and November.
2026 marks the pioneer Grade 10 cohort entering Senior Secondary School (SSS) under the 2-6-3-3-3 CBC structure.

faq.question: How many school terms does Kenya have?
faq.answer: Kenya has 3 school terms per year: Term 1 (January–April), Term 2 (May–August), and Term 3 (August/September–October/November). Each term has a mid-term break, and there are longer holidays between terms.

faq.question: When do Kenya schools open in 2026?
faq.answer: In 2026, Term 1 runs from January 5 to April 2, 2026 (13 weeks). Term 2 runs from April 27 to July 31, 2026 (14 weeks). Term 3 runs from August 24 to October 23, 2026 (10 weeks), followed by national examinations.

faq.question: When is the December holiday for schools?
faq.answer: The long December holiday typically runs from early November to early January — about 9 weeks. It's the longest school break in the Kenyan calendar.

faq.question: Do all schools follow the same term dates?
faq.answer: Public schools follow the Ministry of Education's official calendar. Private and international schools may set their own calendars, though most align closely with the MoE dates.

faq.question: Is solar worth it in Kenya?
faq.answer: Yes. Kenya sits on the equator with excellent year-round sunlight (5.3–6.5 kWh/m²/day). Most grid-tied solar systems pay for themselves in 3–6 years and generate free electricity for 20+ years after that.

faq.question: How much does a solar system cost in Kenya?
faq.answer: The average cost is approximately KES 80,000 per kilowatt (kW) installed for a grid-tied system including panels, inverter, mounting, and installation. A typical household might need a 2–5 kW system (KES 160,000–400,000).

faq.question: How many solar panels do I need for my home?
faq.answer: It depends on your electricity consumption. A household spending KES 5,000/month on KPLC tokens typically needs a 2–3 kW system (6–10 panels of 330W each).

faq.question: What is the payback period for solar in Kenya?
faq.answer: Typically 3–6 years depending on your location, system size, and current electricity spending. After payback, you enjoy 15–20 more years of free electricity.

faq.question: Do solar panels work during the rainy season?
faq.answer: Yes, but at reduced efficiency. Solar panels still generate electricity on cloudy days, typically at 10–30% of their rated capacity. Kenya's rainy seasons are relatively short (March–May and Oct–Dec).

notes: Stamp duty is payable within 30 days of execution of the transfer instrument
First-time buyers under the Affordable Housing Fund (AHF) scheme are exempt from stamp duty
LSK conveyancing fees are calculated on a progressive scale similar to tax bands
Land rent and rates clearance are additional county-specific costs for leasehold properties

faq.question: What is stamp duty in Kenya?
faq.answer: Stamp duty is a government tax charged on the transfer of property (land or buildings) in Kenya. It is payable to the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) within 30 days of executing the transfer instrument.

faq.question: What is the stamp duty rate for urban vs rural property?
faq.answer: Stamp duty is 4% of the market value for urban and peri-urban properties, and 2% for rural properties. First-time buyers under the Affordable Housing Fund (AHF) scheme are fully exempt.

faq.question: What are conveyancing fees in Kenya?
faq.answer: Conveyancing fees are legal fees paid to an advocate for handling the property transfer process. Rates are set by the Law Society of Kenya (LSK) Advocates Remuneration Order on a progressive scale based on property value.

faq.question: Are first-time home buyers exempt from stamp duty?
faq.answer: Yes. Under the Affordable Housing Fund (AHF) scheme introduced in Finance Act 2023, first-time buyers of affordable housing units are exempt from stamp duty entirely.

faq.question: What other costs are involved in property transfer?
faq.answer: Beyond stamp duty and conveyancing fees, you may also need to pay: Land Registry registration fee (KES 5,000 flat), search fee (KES 520), consent to transfer (KES 5,000), valuation fee (~0.25% of property value), and county-specific land rates clearance.

KIPI processes applications on a first-come-first-served basis

faq.question: How much does it cost to register a trademark in Kenya?
faq.answer: The total KIPI fees for registering a trademark in one class are approximately KES 22,450. This includes search (KES 1,000), application (KES 3,850), examination (KES 5,500), Gazette publication (KES 3,300), registration (KES 7,700), and certificate (KES 1,100). Attorney fees are separate.

faq.question: How long does trademark registration take in Kenya?
faq.answer: Trademark registration typically takes 12–18 months from application to certificate issuance. This includes the 60-day opposition period after Gazette publication.

faq.question: What are trademark classes?
faq.answer: The Nice Classification divides goods and services into 45 classes (34 goods, 11 services). You need to register in each class relevant to your business. Each additional class costs KES 3,080 on top of the base application fee.

faq.question: What is the difference between a patent and a utility model?
faq.answer: A patent protects novel inventions for 20 years and requires thorough examination (costs ~KES 34,650). A utility model (petty patent) is simpler, faster (6–12 months), cheaper (~KES 13,750), but only lasts 10 years and has a lower inventiveness threshold.

faq.question: Do I need an IP attorney?
faq.answer: While not strictly required for Kenyan nationals, using a registered IP agent/attorney is highly recommended. They handle the technical filing process and respond to KIPI queries. Foreign applicants must use a registered Kenyan IP agent.

faq.question: What is the fine for speeding in Kenya?
faq.answer: Speeding fines range from KES 5,000 for exceeding the limit by up to 10 km/h, to KES 50,000 for exceeding by over 40 km/h. Higher speed offences also carry more demerit points and may result in arrest.

faq.question: What is the NTSA demerit points system?
faq.answer: Kenya uses a 24-point demerit system over a 3-year period. Points 1–12 result in a warning, 13–18 require a mandatory road safety course, 19–23 lead to license suspension for 6 months, and 24+ points result in license revocation.

faq.question: What is the fine for driving without insurance in Kenya?
faq.answer: Driving without valid motor vehicle insurance carries a fine of up to KES 50,000 and is an arrestable offence. You can also face imprisonment. Insurance is a legal requirement under Cap 405.

faq.question: How do I pay NTSA traffic fines?
faq.answer: You can pay via: cash bond at the police station, M-Pesa paybill (NTSA service), eCitizen portal (ntsa.go.ke), or through court-imposed fine after a hearing.

faq.question: What is the fine for drunk driving in Kenya?
faq.answer: First offence DUI carries a fine of KES 100,000 plus license suspension for 1 year or imprisonment up to 2 years. Repeat offenders face KES 200,000 fine plus license revocation and up to 3 years imprisonment.

notes: Third Party Only insurance is the minimum legal requirement under the Insurance (Motor Vehicle Third Party Risks) Act (Cap 405)
Driving without valid insurance is a criminal offence with a fine of up to KES 100,000 or imprisonment

faq.question: Is vehicle insurance mandatory in Kenya?
faq.answer: Yes. Third Party Only insurance is the minimum legal requirement under the Insurance (Motor Vehicle Third Party Risks) Act (Cap 405). Driving without valid insurance is a criminal offence with a fine of up to KES 100,000 or imprisonment.

faq.question: What is the minimum car insurance cost in Kenya?
faq.answer: The minimum Third Party Only insurance for a private vehicle is KES 7,500 per year. This covers injury/death to third parties and damage to third party property, but does not cover your own vehicle.

faq.question: What is the difference between Third Party and Comprehensive insurance?
faq.answer: Third Party Only covers damage to other people and their property. Comprehensive cover additionally protects your own vehicle against damage, theft, fire, and windscreen breakage. Comprehensive premiums are typically 4–6% of your vehicle's value.

faq.question: Who sets minimum insurance premiums in Kenya?
faq.answer: The Insurance Regulatory Authority (IRA) sets minimum premium rates for all motor insurance categories. Actual premiums from insurance companies may be higher based on the insurer's risk assessment and your driving history.

faq.question: Do boda bodas need insurance?
faq.answer: Yes. Motorcycles (including boda bodas) require at least Third Party Only insurance with a minimum premium of KES 4,000/year. This is enforced by NTSA and traffic police.

faq.question: How many constituencies are in Kenya?
faq.answer: Kenya has 290 parliamentary constituencies, distributed across 47 counties. Each constituency elects one Member of Parliament (MP) to the National Assembly.

faq.question: How many wards are in Kenya?
faq.answer: Kenya has 1,450 wards. Each ward elects a Member of County Assembly (MCA) who represents residents in the county assembly.

faq.question: When is the next general election in Kenya?
faq.answer: The next general election in Kenya is scheduled for August 2027. The current elected officials (2022 cycle) serve a 5-year term.

faq.question: What does an MP, Senator, and Governor do?
faq.answer: An MP represents a constituency in the National Assembly and makes national laws. A Senator represents a county in the Senate and protects county interests. A Governor heads the county executive and manages county services and development.

faq.question: How is my water bill calculated in Kenya?
faq.answer: Water bills in Kenya use a step-function (block) tariff. You pay a lower rate for the first few cubic metres (lifeline tariff), and the rate increases as your consumption rises. A sewerage surcharge (typically 75% of the water charge) and fixed meter rent are added.

faq.question: What is the lifeline tariff?
faq.answer: The lifeline tariff is a subsidized rate for the first 0–6 cubic metres of water consumed per month. It ensures basic water access for low-income households at a very low cost (typically KES 33–45 per m³ under WASREB domestic tariff bands).

faq.question: How much water does an average Kenyan household use?
faq.answer: An average household of 4–5 people in Nairobi uses approximately 10–20 cubic metres (m³) per month. This covers cooking, cleaning, bathing, and laundry. Households with gardens or larger families may use 30+ m³.

faq.question: Why is there a sewerage charge?
faq.answer: The sewerage charge covers wastewater treatment and sewer network maintenance. It's calculated as a percentage (usually 75%) of your water consumption charge. Properties not connected to the sewer network may be exempt.

faq.question: Which body regulates water tariffs in Kenya?
faq.answer: The Water Services Regulatory Board (WASREB) approves all water and sewerage tariffs in Kenya. Individual water utilities (like NCWSC for Nairobi) propose tariffs, and WASREB approves them after public consultation.
